planting.note: Plant deep, burying the lowest leaf node, to encourage a resilient root crown.

directions: This late large-flowered climber opens star-shaped white blooms tinged yellow, with pale greenish-yellow bars running down each sepal, over a long summer-to-autumn season. It earned an RHS Award of Garden Merit following a multi-year Wisley trial of late large-flowered clematis. Give it rich, well-drained soil with a cool, shaded root zone and a sunnier top growth area, and prune hard in late winter as a Group 3 clematis.

planting.note: Site where lower stems stay shaded while the vine climbs into sun.

directions: Bred by Wim Snoeijer in the Jackmanii group and marketed under the trade name Happy Birthday, this cultivar opens deep purple with a redder mid-stripe and matures toward cobalt-blue as the six broad sepals age. It received a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit in a late large-flowered clematis trial at Wisley. Grow it as a Group 3 (hard-prune) clematis on a trellis or through a shrub, cutting all stems back to a low bud in late winter.

planting.note: Shade the base of the vine with low companion plants or mulch.

directions: A late large-flowered clematis with deeply textured, crimped sepals in a rich raspberry-pink that pales on the reverse, set off by pale yellow anthers on cream filaments from late summer into autumn. It holds a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit from a Wisley trial of late large-flowered cultivars. Prune as Group 3, cutting all growth back hard in late winter, and let it climb a sunny trellis or obelisk with cool, moist roots.

planting.note: Good candidate for a large container with a short trellis.

directions: Part of Raymond Evison's compact Boulevard collection, this dwarf climber opens lavender flowers with pink mid-veins and white-and-maroon stamens, fading to a soft silvery lavender as they age. Bloom lasts unusually long, from early summer into autumn, well beyond the one-to-two-month window typical of most clematis. Its short, manageable habit suits patio pots and small gardens; keep roots shaded and cool while letting the vine reach for sun, and prune lightly as a Group 2 clematis.

planting.note: Compact enough for container culture on a small trellis.

directions: Launched as a new introduction from Raymond Evison's Guernsey breeding programme and named for the Tumaini Fund charity in Tanzania, this compact clematis produces a dense profusion of mauve-purple flowers with darker pink centers and a mauve band along each sepal's midrib. Main bloom comes in late spring and early summer, often with a second flush in early autumn. It is well suited to pots and small-space gardens; keep the root zone cool and shaded, give the vine sun to climb into, and prune lightly in late winter.

planting.note: Showcased at RHS Chelsea 2024; suited to patio containers or small trellises.

directions: A 2024 Raymond Evison introduction named for Lindsay Reid, former director of Guernsey Clematis Nursery, this clematis carries large star-shaped flowers up to about 5 inches across in deep purple-blue with red anthers, covering the plant from base to tip in late spring through midsummer, with a second round in early autumn. Its modest stature keeps it manageable on a small trellis or in a large pot. Treat as a Group 2 clematis: light pruning only, with cool shaded roots and a sunnier spot for the foliage and flowers.

planting.note: Flute-shaped buds open flat; good for small gardens or front-of-border trellis work.

directions: Another 2024 Evison breeding-programme release, this clematis opens narrow, flute-like buds that unfurl into large pure-white, star-shaped flowers with reddish anthers, blooming from late spring well into early autumn. Its compact, roughly knee-to-waist-high habit fits containers and the front of mixed borders as easily as a small trellis. Keep the roots cool and moist while the vine climbs toward sun, and prune lightly as a Group 2 clematis after the main spring flush.

planting.note: Non-vining habit; stake lightly for height or let it scramble as groundcover.

directions: A cross of the non-vining Clematis x diversifolia (C. integrifolia x C. viticella 'Olgae') with the climber 'The President,' this cultivar forms a sprawling, shrubby mound rather than climbing, producing recurved, deep sapphire-blue to purple flowers with near-black anthers from late spring through early fall. Because it lacks true climbing tendrils, it works equally well mingled through perennial borders, allowed to scramble as groundcover, or loosely corralled against short stakes. It tolerates average garden soil and benefits from a hard cutback in late winter like other Group 3 clematis.
